evidence.paraphrase: A bird that can speak and magically grant wishes is established as part of the story world.
evidence.quote: and soon a little bird came and built its nest upon the tree, and talked with her, and watched over her, and brought her whatever she wished for.

evidence.paraphrase: Ashputtel weeps out of longing to attend the feast.
evidence.quote: she could not help crying, for she thought to herself, she should so have liked to have gone with them to the ball

evidence.paraphrase: Birds respond to her call and sort the peas from the ashes.
evidence.quote: Then first came two white doves, flying in at the kitchen window; next came two turtle-doves; and after them came all the little birds under heaven, chirping and fluttering in: and they flew down into the ashes.

evidence.paraphrase: The bird provides her with fine clothing by magical means.
evidence.quote: Then her friend the bird flew out of the tree, and brought a gold and silver dress for her, and slippers of spangled silk

evidence.paraphrase: A stepsister mutilates her foot to fit the slipper.
evidence.quote: So the silly girl cut off her great toe, and thus squeezed on the shoe

evidence.paraphrase: A dove sings to reveal the deception to the prince.
evidence.quote: and on the branch sat a little dove singing

evidence.paraphrase: The stepmother and sisters react with fear and anger when Ashputtel is chosen.
evidence.quote: But the mother and both the sisters were frightened, and turned pale with anger as he took Ashputtel on his horse
